After FSW at 375rpm-80 mm/min and 400rpm-100 mm/min, the majority of the Fe2(Nb,Mo) Laves phase particles in the SZs are dissolved into the Fe matrix with a few micron-scale bulky ones segregated at grain boundaries (Figs. 9 and 13).

When the rotation speed is increased to 400rpm, more nanoscale precipitates are formed in the SZ, as the dark particles illustrated in BF (Fig. 10 a) and white particles demonstrated in HAADF (Fig. 10 b).

When the welding speed is facilitated to 100 mm/min, on one hand, the equiaxed grains in the SZ are refined, on the other hand, nanoscale precipitates disappear due to the reduced heat input (Fig. 13 a).
First, a 22 kg ingot was cast in a vacuum induction furnace
then it was homogenized at 1100 ◦C for 2 hh
Afterward, the ingot was forged using the residual heat after the previous homogenization treatment.
Subsequently, it was hot-rolled at 1000 ◦C, 800 ◦C, 600 ◦C, and 400 ◦C to produce plates with a final thickness of 1.7 mm. The total thickness reduction was ~80%.
After that, the plates were annealed at 650 ◦C for 1 hh to activate the microstructure recovery.
